expected_what.value: An engineer deploys an emergency production fix immediately and logs it in the change management tool; the change then goes to the CAB for post-implementation approval.

expected_who.value: The deploying engineer initiates the emergency change. The CAB - the Change Manager (P. Naidoo) plus two other senior engineers - performs the post-implementation approval.

expected_when.value: Deployment happens immediately when needed; CAB approval is targeted within 2 business days after deployment.

expected_why.value: Waiting for CAB approval before an emergency fix would worsen the production outage, so the fix happens first and independent review confirms appropriateness shortly afterward.

expected_where.value: The change management tool: a ticket for the emergency change itself, and a separate approval record once CAB signs off.

expected_how.value: CAB reviews what was changed, why, whether it worked, and whether a follow-up standard change request is needed for a permanent fix.

expected_design_rationale: As DESIGNED, the control is coherent: a fast fix followed by a defined, independent post-implementation review within a stated SLA, with a clear rationale for the after-the-fact sequencing. All six attributes are established from a consistent account. This case is not about a design flaw - see expected_gap_indicator for the separate operating-effectiveness issue this walkthrough surfaces.

expected_risk_objective_control_alignmen.rationale: The two-step design (immediate fix, then independent CAB review) directly addresses the risk of unauthorized or untested emergency changes going undetected, consistent with the stated control objective.

expected_gap_indicator.description: Of the last 6 emergency changes this quarter, only 2 have a completed CAB post-implementation approval record; the other 4 remain open, one over three weeks past the 2-business-day SLA, with no escalation or tracking mechanism for overdue approvals (L11-L14). The control is well designed but is not operating effectively as executed.

reviewer_notes: This is the pilot's 'design is fine, execution is not' case - a negative control for missing-information detection (nothing here should be flagged as missing; all six attributes are answered) paired with a genuine, textually-explicit operating gap that only a design-vs-operation distinction can catch. expected_gap_indicator is ground truth for when gap-assessment logic is eventually built; it is not asserted through the current schema's design_assessment, which only speaks to design, not operating effectiveness.
